issues: No factual error found. Every element of the correction matches Röhr's thesis (pp. 58-60): the taz 'TUWAT,TXT' notice of 1 September 1981 (footnote 319: taz, 01. September 1981, S. 2), the meeting called for 12.9.81 at the taz building in Berlin (Wattstr.), the signature 'Tom Twiddlebit, Wau Wolf Ungenannt(»2)', the names Schleisiek, Holland-Moritz, Gevert, Müller and Büttner, and 'die fünf einladenden Hamburger'.

Minor hedge: the thesis reports the attendance as hearsay ('sollen etwa 20 Personen gekommen sein' = 'about 20 people are said to have come'). The correction's 'about 20 people attended' is acceptable and needs no change.

Verdict MISLEADING (rather than FALSE) is right. The CCC itself calls the 1981 meeting only an 'informelle Gründung'. The Wau Holland Foundation calls him 'doyen and co-founder', though the same page also says 'Through founding the Chaos Computer Club in 1981, Wau Holland...', which is the sole-founder shorthand this myth corrects. Röhr also records that the club set up its registered association (e.V.) only in spring 1986 ('gründete der Club im Frühjahr 1986 einen eingetragenen Verein').

issues: The claim, verdict (MISLEADING) and correction all hold. Barlow's own 2016 account says he wrote the piece at 'a staff party for the closing of the World Economic Forum', for the book 24 Hours in Cyberspace, whose editors 'found it too controversial to include'. It also says he 'sent it out the next day to the 600 or so friends I had with e-mail addresses'. Wired (Andy Greenberg, 2016-02-08) confirms the story independently: it was written at a party on the last night of the 1996 WEF in Davos, 'in one of the hotel's side rooms', as a contribution to '24 Hours In Cyberspace'. EFF's canonical text carries the dateline 'Davos, Switzerland February 8, 1996'. Nothing shows it was ever delivered as a speech.

Minor, in source 1 only: the note on the Doctorow source calls it 'the accurate framing'. But Doctorow's phrase 'where he'd been addressing world leaders' is not supported by Barlow's own account (he says WEF brought in wired types 'mostly as curiosities') or by Wired (he 'spent the previous four days in Davos listening ... to world leaders'). The Doctorow line is better presented as a secondary account that already leans toward the 'speaking to world leaders' framing, while still describing a written document. The note is corrected below; the record's fields need no change.

Checked the date: Barlow's Boing Boing post has datePublished 2016-02-09T03:31Z, which is the evening of 8 Feb in US time; the URL slug is /2016/02/08/ and the text says 'Twenty years ago tonight'. The record date of 2016-02-08 is fine.

Quote FOUND verbatim. Byline (author meta) is Cory Doctorow, and datePublished is 2016-02-08T16:06Z. Caution: this is a secondary account. Its 'where he'd been addressing world leaders' is not corroborated by Barlow's own reflection, where WEF brought in 'a few wired types like myself, mostly as curiosities', or by Wired 2016, where he 'spent the previous four days in Davos listening ... to world leaders'. It correctly says he 'sat down ... and wrote' a document, not that he gave a speech. It shows how the story drifts toward 'addressing world leaders'; it is not a fully accurate framing.
